commits.message:
feat: OKLCH per-axis mix and ΔE; powerline seams stay visible between near-equal backgrounds (#153)

* feat(oklch): mixAxes moves each axis its own share; mix is its uniform case

* fix(oklch): mixAxes checks its four axes by name, mix reports t, one shared interpolation; docs and independent tests

* feat(oklch): deltaE — OKLab distance (CSS Color 4 deltaEOK)

* feat(strip): powerline draws the divider between neighbours whose backgrounds the eye cannot tell apart

* fix(strip): the powerline arrow and its divider are one pair; palette colours compare by slot

A caller replacing only the glyph (">" for ASCII) kept the U+E0B1 divider
beside it, which renders as tofu without a powerline font. PowerlineJoinerOptions
now requires both; the unset case is the exported POWERLINE_JOINER_GLYPHS pair.

indistinct() compared valueless colours by name, so "red" and "color(1)" —
one palette slot — were two colours. It compares type + number now.

* fix(strip): new PowerlineJoiner() draws POWERLINE_JOINER_GLYPHS, not a second copy of it

* fix(strip): seams measured as drawn (alpha flattened); frozen default pair; docs name the divider case

Pushback: a plain-JS caller omitting divider — the required pair in
PowerlineJoinerOptions is the contract; a runtime ?? would be the defensive
fallback the pair replaced.
